pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Cippenham School
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions that you will make as a parent. I am delighted that you are considering Cippenham School, it is an incredible place. We are a large five form entry happy, caring, diverse, inclusive school in the middle of Cippenham Village.
The staff and I are committed to ensuring that each child at our school has access to the best possible learning opportunities and experiences, which will then enable them to be the 'best they can be' academically, socially and personally. We want our Year 6 children leaving us as confident young people, prepared for the next stage of their education; ready to be strong citizens of Slough and the world beyond.
Educating children is a great responsibility and privilege and at Cippenham School we readily accept this, working in partnership with our parents and carers.
Visitors often comment on the warm, friendly atmosphere at our school and the positive attitude of the children and staff. If you are interested in finding out more first hand, please book an appointment to visit us. We look forward to welcoming you.

Music at Cippenham School
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity: a subject that enriches children’s lives and education with many benefits beyond itself. It contributes significantly in developing language, reasoning and memory; it allows children to connect with others by creating a sense of community and promoting teamwork; it leads to improved motor skills and co-ordination; it improves memory and integrates many other subjects. In addition music teaches discipline, relieves stress, builds confidence and enhances self-esteem by allowing all children to succeed. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. It should be inclusive and accessible for everyone to be actively involved in their learning. Our curriculum lends itself to broadening student’s knowledge and cultural capital as well as increasing engagement through practical schemes.
Cippenham School understands the value and enrichment music brings to the life of a child and to the school as a community and we recognise that music, as a practical subject, should be an integral part of a rich, broad and balanced curriculum. Children participate in a range of musical experiences throughout their school lives, building up their confidence at the same time and enjoying the performance aspect that music affords. At Cippenhman, music lessons are about learning in and through music, not solely about music, and aim to build pupils’ knowledge and skills as well as developing their imagination and creativity. Children learn how to listen to and appraise music; cultivate their understanding of the Interrelated Dimensions of Music (IDM) such as rhythm, beat, and pitch; acquire technical vocabulary for these musical elements; learn how music is structured and created through practical activities; and develop instrumental and vocal technique through performances and composition. Children’s musical experience is bedded in a broad range of musical styles from a wide spectrum of cultures and eras.

pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be - SEND Provision
pageCache.text:
SEND Provision
Cippenham School aims to support children with special educational needs and disability (SEND) by seeking to remove barriers to learning and participation, ensuring all pupils have access to an appropriate education that affords them the opportunity to achieve their personal potential.
We support children in four main areas:
communication and interaction
cognition and learning
behaviour, emotional and social development
sensory and/or physical.
We work collaboratively with outside agencies ensuring specialist advice and provision supports effective teaching and learning.
What is the Local Offer?
In September 2014 the government made a lot of changes to the way that children and young people aged 0 to 25, with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are supported. This included making Local Authorities produce a ‘ SEND Local Offer’.
The SEND Local Offer aims to bring together helpful and useful information for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities and their families. It is a comprehensive guide to services and support all in one place. Please watch the video at the bottom of this page to find out more.
You can find Slough’s Local Offer here.
You can find our Extended Local Offer Response here.
Policies and reports
You can find our SEND policy on our dedicated policies page.
For further information about what we do, or for any support, please contact our SEN Admin Assistant via email: office@cippenhamschool.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be - Remote & Home Learning
pageCache.text:
Remote & Home Learning
Our pupils can access learning from home in a variety of ways - please see our Remote Learning policy on our policies page.
We may provide learning via Google Classroom - your child has a login set up for this which is typically found in their reading record.
Please find other useful websites and applications below for you child to access remotely.
Home Learning Websites
Times Table Rock Stars
Learning and understanding the times tables is a challenging but fundamental part of the mathematics curriculum. Pupils who have a deep understanding of these facts are typically more confident when learning new concepts.
Times Table Rock Stars helps pupils to learn the times table and their associated division facts in a gradual, systematic format. Individual programmes can be set up to ensure they are guided through at their own pace. Most importantly, it presents the learning in a fun and competitive style.
NumBots
At Cippenham, we want all pupils to be able to understand, recall and be fluent in mental calculations in addition and subtraction. NumBots is a platform which develops the knowledge and skills of pupils so that they begin to see the relationships between numbers, learn efficient strategies and move from counting to calculating.
It is a highly engaging platform for students in both KS1 and KS2 - characters can be adapted as the story mode in the game progresses.
Reading Eggs
Reading Eggs makes learning to read interesting and engaging for kids, with great online reading games and activities.
Educational Websites

A timed, fast paced maths game with different concepts to focus on.

pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be - WrapAround Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Kidz Enterprise
The school offers wraparound care for students from Reception to Year 6 through Kidz Enterprise. Families can register their child's place via their website here.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club is the perfect answer to parents starting work early and in need of childcare prior to school opening hours.
Kidz Enterprise provides a warm welcoming environment and operates each morning from 7.30am to the start of school, with a healthy selection of breakfast available until 8:10am.
Children who attend the Breakfast Club have the opportunity to participate in a wide range of activities that include group games and quieter activities for those that wish to chill out before school. Activities are planned to help children learn, play and relax with their friends, making full use of outside facilities.
Each morning we offer a breakfast special that may include Crumpets, Waffle, Bagel, Crumpets, Fruit Loaf, Pancakes, in addition to the special we also offer a selection of Cereals, Toast, Fruit Juice, Milk, Water and Fruit.
After School Club
The After School Club is available each afternoon from school finish until 6pm and offers at no extra cost a basic healthy snack which includes a wide range of seasonal fruits and vegetables on a daily basis.
Our trained staff take a genuine interest in your child's development, helping with homework and listening to your child read helping to take the stress away from parents once they get home.
Children who attend the After School Club are able to participate in a wide range of activities that include sports, art & craft, cookery and table games, the club has use of a bouncy castle that is available for the children to use on a regular basis. Activities are planned to help children learn, play and relax with their friends, making full use of outside facilities at all times of the year.
Parents can pick up at any time up until 6pm. All children must be signed out by an adult over 16 who is named on that child’s registration form.
Each afternoon we offer a snack special that may include Pizza Slice, Beans on Toast, Spaghetti on Toast, Soup, or snacks where the children can be supported by staff to make their own Wrap, Bagel or Sandwich with fillings that may include Cheese, Ham, Jam, Marmite, Tuna Mayo, Chicken and Cheese Spread.
Each afternoon we also have a selection of vegetables and seasonal fruits available along with Water.
Food And Snacks at Kidz Enterprise
A snack is available for children from school finish till about 4.30pm so children can decide when to eat. Healthy Eating Guidelines are followed and includes wraps or sandwiches with cheese or meat, vegetables, fruit and yogurt. Children who attend clubs after school are offered a snack when they arrive at the club.
**Please note: all Clubs are nut-free zones.**

pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be - New Starters Information
pageCache.text:
New Starter Information
Welcome to Cippenham School
Thank you for choosing us as your child's school. We want to ensure that every child's experience of education gives them a good start to a lifetime of learning.
We understand that starting your child at school can be a nervous time and hope that the information you find here will be useful. The office team are always happy to help if you have any queries not dealt with here
Do look out for information from our excellent 'Friends of Cippenham School' who run successful social events for all of our new parents to help you quickly feel part of our community.
Helpful Hints
Here is some information, which you might find useful:
Your child can come into school between 8.35am and 8.45am. Children arriving after this will be recorded as late in the register.
If your child is unwell, please contact the school office on 01628 604665 each morning to let us know. If you have booked a school lunch please cancel it.
All children in YR, 1 and 2 are provided with a piece of fresh fruit or vegetable each day. Please ensure additional foods from home are ‘Healthy Snacks’ and nut and orange free. Milk is provided for all children under 5.
We have a number of children who are allergic to nuts, and / or sesame seeds, and oranges, please do not pack products with these ingredients for lunch or snacks
School finishes at 3.15pm.
The school has extended day care running from Monday to Friday from 7.30am to 6pm. Please contact Kidz Club Enterprise for further information and to book.
If your child requires any prescription medicine while they are in school, we ask that you complete a medication administration request (see below), and leave this and the medicine in the school office.
Newsletters are issued weekly. They are emailed to parents where we have an email address, and are also available on the school’s website.
We use a text service to contact parents (ie to advise about an unexpected school closure, or a reminder about an event or class assembly etc), an email service (for newsletters etc). Please work with us and ensure that we always have an up-to-date contact information for you.
Term dates can be found under the School Life tab. Please contact the school office if you require any of the information or forms in hard copy. Thank you.
School Lunches
Children in Foundation, Year 1 and Year 2 can have a school lunch at no cost to their parents. Pupils do not need to be registered for this - parents just need to order lunches on the three week menus available from the school office, the website or the children's book bags. This scheme is known as Universal Free School Meals (or UFSM)
Children in other school years may also be eligible for free school meals (FSM) if their parent is receiving qualifying welfare benefits. Pupils who qualify for FSM also qualify for a Pupil Premium Grant (PPG). This is (currently) an extra £1,300 for the school to use to fund valuable support like extra tuition, additional teaching staff or after school activities. This additional money is available from central government for every child whose parent is receiving one of the qualifying welfare benefits, but only is the parents register.. It is therefore important that eligible families sign up for free school meals, even if their child is in Foundation, Year 1 or Year 2, i.e. a year group that receives Universal Free School Meals.
To check your eligibility please use the following link: https://www.slough.gov.uk/education-help-financial-support/free-school-meals
The Pupil Premium is funding allocated to schools for the specific purpose of boosting the attainment of pupils from low-income families. You can read our latest funding statement here.
Funding is based on children who have been registered for free school meals at any time in the last 6 years, further reinforcing the importance of making sure all those who qualify are actually registered. Even if you (or your child) don't want to receive free school meals on a regular basis, there may be other educational benefits for them through the Pupil Premium. Your child(ren) can have a free school meal any day they choose. Taking up free school meals has many benefits:
Your child(ren) will benefit from a eating a free healthy nutritious meal and families could be saving more than £400 per child per year,
Schools also benefit directly by receiving money from the government. The government pays schools £1,300 for every primary child and £935 for every secondary child who registers for free school meals plus additional funding through the schools' budget. This means there may be help available for you with the cost residential school trips, travel costs to school, or help with school uniform costs.
Before and After School Care
At Cippenham School we aim to support working parents in the best possible way. We offer care for children from 7.30am until 6pm in the evening from Monday to Friday with Kidz Enterprise Ltd. The care is run on the school site and led by Mr Derek Beasley.
Further information can be found here.
The club can be booked on line here.

Parent Support
Cost of living - Help & Advice
Many people are worried about money at the moment, important costs like energy, food and fuel are rising steeply. If you're worried about being able to afford to live, you're not alone and there is support available.
You can get advice and support offering signposting to groups for support with food, energy, skills and more.
Slough Borough Council
Food services and support
Not Just Community Store
Free School Meals
Do you receive any of the following support?
Universal Credit (provided you have an annual net earned income of no more than £7,400, as assessed by earnings from up to three of your most recent assessment periods)
Income-based Jobseeker's Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The guarantee element of Pension Credit
Child Tax Credit (provided you're not also entitled to Working Tax Credit and have an annual gross income of no more than £16,190)
Working Tax Credit run-on - paid for four weeks after you stop qualifying for Working Tax Credit
If you can answer yes to any of the above you may qualify for free school meals/Pupil Premium.
If your application is successful not only will your child receive free school meals, but our school will receive additional funding.
Free School Meal Letter
Pupil Premium Poster
To check if your child is eligible, please visit the following link:
https://www.cloudforedu.org.uk/ofsm/sims-elliotfoundation
Food Voucher
If your children are eligible for benefit related free school meals*, they could be entitled to food vouchers during the school holidays.
*not to be confused with universal free school meals for children in Reception, Year 1 and Year2.
To check if your child is eligible, please visit the following link:
https://www.cloudforedu.org.uk/ofsm/sims-elliotfoundation
Head lice Advice
Head lice is often a recurring problem in primary schools. We encourage parents to please check their child’s head regularly and if they find head lice please treat as soon as possible and there's no need to keep your child off school if they have head lice.
Head lice School Letter
For more information on how to check and treat head lice click here

pageCache.pageTitle: Be the best you can be - Storm our Well-being Dog
pageCache.text:
Storm: Our Well-being Dog
Why have a School Well-being Dog?
There are many benefits to having a well-being dog in a school setting, the main one being the health and well-being of both pupils and staff alike. A dog has an immediate calming effect by just being near. Storm is calm, affectionate and very gentle natured. She is a much loved staff member now and an integral part of the Cippenham School family.
Benefits of Well-being Dogs
teach empathy and appropriate interpersonal skills
help individuals develop social skills
be soothing and the presence of animals can more quickly build rapport between the teacher and pupil, and improve individual’s skills to pick up social cues imperative to human relationships.
Research into the effects of well-being dogs in schools is showing a range of benefits including:
increase in school attendance
decreases in learner anxiety behaviours resulting in improved learning outcomes, such as increases in reading and writing levels
positive changes towards learning and improved motivation, and enhanced relationships with peers and teachers due to experiencing trust and unconditional love from a therapy dog. This in turn helps pupils learn how to express their feelings and enter into more trusting relationships.
Storm will continue her regular visits, coming in once or twice a week to spend time with the children and staff. She is known for her wagging tail, and the more excited she is, the more her tail wags. Storm is continuing her training as a therapy dog and is an incredibly calming but enjoyable experience for the children.
If your child is worried by having Storm in school, please let us know and we can ensure that Storm is kept away.
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
What if my child is allergic to dogs?
It is understandable that some parents/carers may be concerned about possible allergic reactions to a school dog. Storm is subjected to the most thorough cleanliness and grooming regime. She will only be in contact with children who voluntarily wish to work/play with her.
What if my child is scared of dogs?
Some children may have had upsetting experiences and have a fear of dogs (or another animal). Experience and research has shown that, with proper guidance and handling, children can learn to overcome their fear of animals and grow in respect and appreciation for them. We have already had this happen with parents and children at our school. Parents have the right to ask that their child/children do not have contact with Storm, but equally the child may like to meet them with the parents present. This can be arranged with Mrs Virk.
Is the dog properly cared for?
Storm is extremely well looked after. Storm lives with Mrs Virk and her family. The days Storm is not at school she is at Doggy Day Care. Storm comes into once a week but sometimes twice if the children have requested her to do so for a special event. Storm will always be accompanied by a trained adult. Whilst Storm is in school she will have access to a dog bed and very comfy chairs in Mrs Virk and the Pastoral office. This is where she can rest and have quiet time. Storm does visit the vet regularly for all her treatments as well as regular check ups. If Storm is not well, Storm stays and home to rest.
Will the school still have a 'no dogs' policy?
Yes. Our school continues with a ‘no dogs’ policy. Attending school dogs/therapy dogs do not fall within the remit of this policy as they are subject to rules as part of our risk assessment. Storm will be on a lead at all times when away from Mrs Virk, near children moving around the school site. Storm will always be accompanied by a trained adult. We will make sure that Storm does not leave any mess in or around our school.
Storm's Risk Assessment
